 EPFO withdrawal and minimum balance rules changed: Salaried employees can withdraw up to 90% of EPF balance
 Personal Finance News
 EPFO withdrawal and minimum balance rules changed: Salaried employees can withdraw up to 90% of EPF balance
 By Ayush Khar 3 min read | Updated on November 21, 2026, 08:09 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 On November 19, 2026, the EPFO approved a proposal to reduce the minimum balance requirement for subscribers to 10% from the pre-existing 25% mandate.
 EPFO subscribers will be able to access a larger portion of their provident fund corpus. | Image: Shutterstock
 The 240th meeting of the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the Employees Provident Fund Organisation ( EPFO ) was held in New Delhi on November 19, 2026. Union Minister for Labour and Employment Mansukh Mandaviya chaired the high-level meeting. The meeting was also attended by Labour Secretary Chandra Bhushan Kumar, Central Provident Fund Commissioner Ramesh Krishnamurthi, and various representatives from state governments along with other stakeholders such as employers, and employee unions.

 Following the meeting, the ministry announced that the EPFO has approved a proposal to reduce the compulsory minimum balance requirement in provident fund accounts from 25% to 10%. Notably, the minimum balance requirement refers to a restriction applied by the EPFO on the amount of money you can withdraw from your total EPF corpus.
 The amendment to the minimum balance requirement frees up, up to 90% of the provident fund corpus for eligible partial withdrawals, before an employee completes 55 years of age. Typically partial withdrawals from the balance are allowed in certain specific cases which are broadly classified as essential needs, housing needs and other special circumstances.
 Some common cases under essential needs in which partial withdrawals are allowed include medical care for yourself or for family members dependent on you, for funding higher education for yourself or for your children and for spending the money on marriage expenses for yourself, your children, or siblings. Similarly, the money can also be withdrawn to buy a house, flat or residential plot, for construction or renovation of an existing home or for repaying a home loan. Other than these, the money can also be withdrawn in certain special circumstances such as losing your job, natural calamities or public health emergencies and for urgent personal emergencies.
 Given the relaxation in maintaining the minimum balance, EPFO subscribers will be able to access a larger portion of their provident fund corpus for meeting critical financial needs ranging from medical emergencies to milestone developments such as marriages. This in turn can aid salaried employees in planning their finances better as they will be able to use a larger share of their provident fund savings for meeting their current needs.
 Prior to the amendment, subscribers were bound by a more stringent rule which mandated them to maintain 25% of their account contributions in the provident fund corpus. The 25% minimum balance provision was conceptualised during the 238th CBT meeting and was formally enacted through the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 2026 on June 29, 2026.
 According to the Ministry of Labour and Employment, the amendment in minimum balance requirement is expected to provide greater financial flexibility to EPF members while safeguarding their long-term social security interests. According to EPFO data the decision directly is set to benefit over 30 crore formal sector workers across the country who rely on their provident fund savings.
